newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks seen weak, focus on politics.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks seen weak, focus on politics.

text.p: Bombay blue chips are likely to remain subdued at start on Tuesday, weighed down by a sharp fall in prices in the previous session on news that a regional party plans to pull out of the minority government, traders said.
But any downside would be limited as foreign funds are expected to turn bargain hunters at lower levels, they said.

"Monday's slide was mainly caused by speculator selling, but this could also be a good oppportunity for funds to pick up stocks available at cheaper rates," said a dealer at a foreign securities firm.
The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagan (DMK) party said on Monday it plans to pull out of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's government, citing differences with coalition partners.
But the DMK party of Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said it would continue to provide support to the government from the outside, despite the pull-out.
The government faced no immediate threat, but adverse political news during a bull run had acted as a market dampener.
A nominal fall in the Bombay index forced stocks to close in negative territory last week -- the first time since May 23.
